message.content:
Below is a quick “recipe” you can drop into most REST‑API clients (Postman, curl, etc.) or even paste straight into a browser address bar if the service supports GET queries. It pulls **only** the `id` and its associated `context` field from the *historical* WHOIS table for `domain6.xyz`, caps the result set at eight records, and asks the server to return the payload in the **“key_def”** representation (a lightweight key/value map). --- ### 1️⃣ Build the HTTP Request | Component | Value | |-----------|-------| | Method | `GET` | | Endpoint | `/api/whois/history` *(adjust based on your provider’s base URL)* | | Query Params | `domain=domain6.xyz`
`fields=id,context`
`limit=8`
`output_format=key_def` | #### Example cURL command ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://your-whois-service.com/api/whois/history?domain=domain6.xyz&fields=id%2Ccontext&limit=8&output_format=key_def" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` > ⚠️ Replace `https://your-whois-service.com/…` with the actual host/path exposed by your WHOIS historian. If authentication is required (e.g., Bearer token), add it via the header: ```bash -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" ``` --- ### 2️⃣ Expected Response Format (`key_def`) A typical `key_def` payload looks like this: ```json { "results": [ { "id": "12345", "context": "Registrar A – March 2019" }, { "id": "67890", "context": "Registrar B – July 2020" }, ... ], "meta": { "count": 8, "query_time_ms": 12 } } ``` Only two keys appear per record—exactly what you asked for: - `"id"` – the unique identifier assigned to each historic snapshot - `"context"` – human‑readable description (often registrar + timestamp) No other columns (like registrant names, dates, status flags, etc.) will surface unless explicitly requested. --- ### 3️⃣ Quick Validation Script (Python) If you prefer to hit the endpoint programmatically, try this minimal script: ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://your-whois-service.com" payload = { "domain": "domain6.xyz", "fields": ["id", "context"], "limit": 8, "output_format": "key_def" } headers = {"Accept": "application/json"} # Add auth headers if needed resp = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/api/whois/history", params=payload, headers=headers) data = resp.json() print("Fetched {} entries".format(len(data["results"]))) for rec in data["results"]: print(rec["id"], "-", rec["context"]) ``` Run it after installing `requests` (`pip install requests`). It prints exactly those two pieces of information for up to eight historical snapshots. --- ### TL;DR Checklist | ✅ | Item | |----|------| | ✔︎ | Target domain: `domain6.xyz` | | ✔︎ | Fields returned: `id`, `context` | | ✔︎ | Result count capped at 8 | | ✔︎ | Output format: `key_def` (compact key/value pairs) | Drop the above request into whatever client you’re comfortable with, tweak the base URL/authentication bits, and you’ll see just the identifiers and their contextual descriptions for the last eight WHOIS changes recorded for `domain6.xyz`.
